findings.evidence: File lines 42-45 vs. PR description: "the only declarations that land here are `ClassGroup.relNorm_comp_map` and `ClassGroup.relNorm_comp_map_eq`, respelt `relNorm_extendedHom` / `relNorm_comp_extendedHom` ... plus their `(Ideal R)⁰`-level step. ... The file's Provenance section records the same." It does not. Repo convention is a per-declaration list: TauCeti/RingTheory/PowerSeries/Order.lean:28-30, TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/SymplecticMultiplier.lean:37.
findings.fix: Add `ClassGroup.relNorm_comp_map` and `ClassGroup.relNorm_comp_map_eq` (and the `(Ideal R)⁰`-level step) to the ported-declarations list at lines 42-45, noting the respelling against Mathlib's `ClassGroup.extendedHom`/`extendedIdeal`, exactly as the description's Provenance section does.
findings.issue: The Provenance declaration list (lines 42-45) still names only `relNorm0`, `mk0CompRelNorm0`, `mk0CompRelNorm0_apply`, `mk0CompRelNorm0_eq_of_mk0_eq`, `ClassGroup.relNorm`, `relNorm_mk0`, `relNorm_mk0'`. The PR's own description states the added `relNorm_extendedHom` / `relNorm_comp_extendedHom` are the source's `ClassGroup.relNorm_comp_map` / `relNorm_comp_map_eq` "respelt" against Mathlib's `extendedHom`, plus their `(Ideal R)⁰`-level step (`Ideal.relNorm0_extendedIdeal`) — so a central source named in the description is not credited in the code for the very declarations the PR adds.

findings.evidence: Lines 38, 63-64, 151 of TauCeti/RingTheory/ClassGroup/RelNorm.lean; PR description Provenance section names these as ported declarations.
findings.fix: Reword all three to say the composite is not in Mathlib but is adapted from the source's `relNorm_comp_map` / `relNorm_comp_map_eq`, so the claim of novelty is scoped to Mathlib and does not displace the source credit.
findings.issue: Three places affirmatively present the composite as original work rather than adapted: line 63 "What remains genuinely new is the composite `relNorm ∘ extendedHom`", line 38 "only this composite is new", and line 151 "Only the composite with `relNorm` is new". Against the description's account these read as new relative to Mathlib only, but in the file — whose Provenance section is the credit mechanism — they assert originality over the AINTLIB source the composite is adapted from.

summary: The file credits the AINTLIB HasseWeil source for the previously ported declarations, but its Provenance section was not updated for the three declarations this PR adds; the file instead calls the composite "genuinely new", contradicting the PR description, which says relNorm_extendedHom / relNorm_comp_extendedHom are respellings of the source's ClassGroup.relNorm_comp_map and relNorm_comp_map_eq.
